<reason>PRO won on scale and fairness. CON's funding/durability dilemma was sharp, but PRO showed tiny bonus uptake cannot fund anything, broad rights create a larger defensive constituency than scattered bonus permits, and CON never answered the two-tier equity charge that exclusion stays where wealthy precincts keep it. Broad eligibility with normal tax-base funding beat funded gradualism that preserves exclusion as the rule.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's B2.3 dilemma - fast growth needs funding vs slow growth makes friction costless - answered by PRO's A4.2-A4.3 that fees still kill small projects and tiny output cannot fund sewers while broad legalization funds via more doors on the tax rolls.</best_rebuttal>
